chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muslim inherits his Zimmi wife, and she does not inherit him.'

key_terms.الذِّمِّيَّةَ: Zimmi wife (a non-Muslim woman, usually Christian or Jewish, under Islamic protection)
key_terms.وَلَا تَرِثُهُ: And she does not inherit him

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim man inherit from his non-Muslim wife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'asymmetry in inheritance' (al-ikhtilaf al-din) by specifying that a Muslim man inherits from his Kitabi (non-Muslim) wife, but she does not inherit from him. This ruling is derived from the general prohibition of Muslim men marrying polytheists, extended here to include People of the Book, and is a key point of discussion among Shia jurists regarding the conditions of the wife's faith at the time of death. It underscores the theological hierarchy where the Muslim's faith takes precedence in financial succession.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallaad who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Muslim inherits his ‘Zimmi’ wife (Jew or a Christian under the protection of Islam), but she does not inherit him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
The Muslim inherits from his Dhimmiy (taxpayer) wife and she cannot inherit from him.’”
